doc.name: A — skincare catalogue, gel lit neon, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: vitamin-C serum dropper bottle
Category: skincare
Shot programme: gel lit neon
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You act as lead photographer and set designer for a skincare catalogue. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the extreme wide set in a gel lit neon treatment.

SUBJECT. A vitamin-C serum dropper bottle. Treat the attached reference as the single source of truth for the product's geometry, proportion, colourway, finish and label typography. Do not redesign, restyle, re-letter or embellish it.

CAMERA. Wide frame with the product small in a large, deliberately empty set. Shoot on a 70-200mm zoom at 150mm at f/22, framing for rule-of-thirds weighting to frame-right.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with flickering firelight as the only motivated source. Stage the product on or against honed travertine, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a clean high-key grade with the whites pushed to the edge of clipping. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Your entire reply is the prompt itself: one dense paragraph, no title, no quotation marks, no trailing notes.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
